Six days ago, Apple released the first developer beta of iOS 27.2, skipping the iOS 27.1 beta. After releasing developer beta 2 yesterday, Apple has now launched the first public beta of iOS 27.2, which includes a brand-new iPhone Health app. Apple has also enabled the feature to schedule and purchase lab testing services through Quest Diagnostics within the new Health app.

iOS 27.2 beta includes updates such as a brand-new Health app

iOS 27.2 will be the next update following the official release of iOS 27 on September 14. iOS 27.1 is only available for the iPhone Duo.

Apple has previously detailed how the iOS 27.1 SDK allows developers to take full advantage of the iPhone Duo's display. You can check here how apps display on the iPhone Duo depending on which iOS version they target.

Apple released Xcode 27.1 beta on Friday, adding an iPhone Duo simulator and app development support for this new foldable iPhone.

The first iOS 27.2 developer beta includes the following changes:

  • The redesigned Health app, first announced by Apple at the iPhone 18 Pro launch event, is now officially enabled in this beta.
  • Dual-camera simultaneous shooting mode arrives on Group FaceTime.
  • Siri AI language support now adds French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.
  • Apple TV app profile feature arrives on iPhone.
  • In Apple Podcasts, "Up Next" has been renamed to "Latest Episode," with the "Continue Playing" section now placed directly below "Latest Episode." The episode list in Podcasts also features backgrounds matching the icon colors.
  • Apple Music now uses fewer icon colors for in-app tags.

iOS 27.2 is expected to officially release in October. Currently, both developer and public betas are available for iPhone users to try out the new Apple Health app ahead of launch.
